questions.question: What is the term used for the line that a raider must cross to score points in Kabaddi?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Baulk line**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In **Kabaddi**, the **Baulk line** is a crucial line that raiders must cross to score points successfully.
 
• The **Baulk line** is located at a distance of **3.75 meters** from the midline of the Kabaddi court in standard matches.
 
• The raider needs to cross this line to validate their raid attempt; failing to do so results in the raid being declared unsuccessful.
 
• Crossing the **Baulk line** helps ensure that the raider makes a genuine attempt to approach the defenders in their half of the court.
 
• Raiders must also return to their half safely after crossing the **Baulk line** to complete a successful raid.
 
• The concept of the **Baulk line** is integral to the rules of Kabaddi, ensuring fair play and strategy during the game.
 
• It is one of the most important markings on the Kabaddi court, alongside the **Bonus line** and **Centre line**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Half line**__

 __
 
• The **Half line**, also referred to as the **Centre line**, divides the Kabaddi court into two equal halves.
 
• It is the starting point for both teams and is used to separate the raiders and defenders during gameplay.
 
 
 
• **Bonus line**__
 __
 
• The **Bonus line** is located parallel to the Baulk line, at a distance of **1 meter** towards the defender’s side.
 
• If a raider crosses the **Bonus line** with one leg while the other remains in the air, they are awarded a bonus point.
 
• The bonus point can only be claimed if at least **6 defenders** are present on the court.
 
 
 
• **Centre line**__
 
 
• The **Centre line** is another term used for the **Half line**, dividing the Kabaddi court into two equal sections.
 
• It marks the starting boundary for raiders at the beginning of each raid.

questions.question: What is the nature of the Concurrent List in the Indian Constitution?

options.text: Both the Centre and the States can legislate

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Both the Centre and the States can legislate**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Concurrent List in the Indian Constitution contains subjects on which both the Centre and the States can legislate.
 
• It is one of the three lists mentioned in the Seventh Schedule of the Constitution, alongside the Union List and State List.
 
• Under Article 246, the Concurrent List allows both levels of government to legislate on matters such as education, marriage, adoption, forests, and criminal law.
 
• If there is a conflict between the laws made by the Centre and the States on any subject in the Concurrent List, the law enacted by Parliament prevails, as per Article 254.
 
• The Concurrent List ensures cooperative federalism, allowing shared responsibility between the Union and State governments for certain matters.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Exclusively for States**

 
 
• The subjects under the State List in the Seventh Schedule are exclusively under the legislative jurisdiction of State governments.
 
• Examples include police, public health, agriculture, and local governance.
 
• States have autonomy in these areas, ensuring decentralized decision-making and governance.
 
 
 
• **Exclusively for Union**
 
 
• The Union List consists of subjects exclusively under the legislative jurisdiction of the Central Government.
 
• Examples include defense, foreign affairs, atomic energy, banking, and currency.
 
• This ensures centralized control over matters of national importance.
 
 
 
• **Only during emergencies**
 
 
• During a National Emergency, the legislative powers of the States can be temporarily overridden by the Central Government.
 
• Under Articles 352, 356, and 360, Parliament can legislate on subjects in the State List during emergencies.
 
• Such provisions ensure effective governance during crises but are limited to the emergency period.

questions.question: Which of the following conditions would result in the fastest evaporation of water from an open container

options.text: Low humidity, high temperature and moving air
High humidity, low temperature and still air
Low humidity, low temperature and moving air
High humidity, high temperature and still air

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Low humidity, high temperature, and moving air**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Evaporation is the process through which liquid water changes into water vapor. It is influenced by factors such as **humidity, temperature, and air movement**.
 
• When **humidity** is low, the surrounding air has a reduced amount of water vapor, allowing more water molecules from the container to escape into the air. *Hence, low humidity enhances evaporation.*
 
• A **high temperature** increases the kinetic energy of water molecules, making them more likely to escape the liquid phase and become vapor. *Thus, high temperature boosts evaporation.*
 
• **Moving air** facilitates evaporation by continuously replacing the saturated air near the water surface with drier air. This helps maintain a high evaporation rate by removing water vapor. *Hence, moving air accelerates evaporation.*
 
• In contrast, **high humidity** and **still air** create an environment where the air is already saturated with water vapor, reducing the potential for evaporation. Similarly, **low temperature** decreases the energy available for water molecules to evaporate. *Thus, these conditions slow down evaporation.*
 
• The combination of **low humidity, high temperature, and moving air** provides the most favorable conditions for the fastest evaporation, as all three factors work together to facilitate the process. *Hence, the correct answer is "Low humidity, high temperature, and moving air".*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Factors Affecting Evaporation:**

 
 
• **Humidity:** High humidity slows evaporation as the air is already saturated with water vapor. Low humidity accelerates evaporation by allowing more water molecules to escape into the atmosphere.
 
• **Temperature:** Higher temperatures increase the kinetic energy of water molecules, enabling them to overcome intermolecular forces and evaporate faster.
 
• **Air Movement:** Moving air replaces saturated air near the water's surface with drier air, maintaining a gradient that promotes evaporation.
 
 
 
• **Real-World Examples:**
 
 
• Clothes dry faster on a sunny, windy day due to the combination of **high temperature, low humidity, and moving air.**
 
• Evaporation rates are higher in arid regions where **humidity** is naturally low.
 
• Industrial cooling towers use **forced air** to enhance evaporation and improve cooling efficiency.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Evaporation:**
 
 
• Evaporation is used in processes like **distillation**, where liquids are separated based on their boiling points.
 
• In agriculture, **evapotranspiration** helps estimate water needs for crops based on evaporation rates.
 
• Evaporation plays a crucial role in water cycle processes such as cloud formation and precipitation.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Evaporation in Daily Life:**

 
 
• Sweat evaporates faster in hot and windy conditions, helping regulate body temperature.
 
• Evaporation is the principle behind cooling mechanisms in air conditioners and refrigerators.
 
 
 
• **Scientific Understanding:**
 
 
• The rate of evaporation depends on the **vapor pressure** of water, which increases with temperature.
 
• Water's **boiling point** is the temperature at which vapor pressure equals atmospheric pressure, resulting in rapid evaporation.

• **Aurangzeb**, also known as **Alamgir**, was the sixth emperor of the **Mughal Empire**. He ruled from **1658 to 1707**.
 
• Aurangzeb expanded the Mughal Empire to its greatest extent, covering almost the entire Indian subcontinent.
 
• He was known for his administrative reforms, military campaigns, and enforcement of Islamic laws. *Hence, he is considered the last powerful Mughal ruler.*
 
• Aurangzeb's reign marked the peak of Mughal power, but it also sowed the seeds of decline due to over-expansion and internal dissent.
 
• His policies and wars strained the empire's resources and created discontent among various groups, including the Rajputs, Marathas, and Sikhs.
 
• After Aurangzeb's death in **1707**, the Mughal Empire gradually weakened, and subsequent rulers failed to maintain the same level of control. *Hence, the correct answer is Aurangzeb.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• He was known for his intellectual pursuits, especially his efforts to bridge Hinduism and Islam. His translation of the **Upanishads** into Persian is noteworthy.
 
• He lost the war of succession to Aurangzeb and was executed in **1659**. Dara Shukoh was not a ruler; hence, this option is incorrect.

• He was a weak ruler and lacked political or military power. His reign marked the end of the Mughal dynasty after British annexation in **1858**. Hence, this option is incorrect.
 
 
 
• **Shah Jahan:**
 
 
• Shah Jahan was the fifth Mughal emperor, ruling from **1628 to 1658**. He is famous for his architectural achievements, including the **Taj Mahal**.
 
• Although he expanded the empire, his reign is more remembered for cultural contributions than political or military dominance. Hence, this option is incorrect.
 
 
 
• **Aurangzeb:**
 
 
• Aurangzeb's reign from **1658 to 1707** was marked by significant territorial expansion, effective administration, and strict implementation of Islamic laws.
 
• His military campaigns extended Mughal control over the Deccan and other regions, making him the last powerful ruler of the empire.

questions.question: A closed cylinder with a base radius of 14 m and height of 21 m is to be made with a metallic sheet of width 20 m. What is the length of sheet required if wastage is negligible? [Use π = (22)/(7)]

**Given:**

A closed cylinder with a base radius, (r) of 14 m and height, (h) of 21 m.

π = (22)/(7)

**Concept Used:**

Total Surface area of Cylinder = 2 π r (r + h)

Length of sheet = Total Surface area/Width of sheet

**Calculation:**

Total Surface area of Cylinder:

⇒ 2 × 22/7 × 14 × (14 + 21)

⇒ 2 × 22/7 × 14 × 35

⇒ 3080 m²

The length of sheet required is,

⇒ 3080/20 = 154 m

**∴ The length of sheet required is 154 m.**

questions.question: A drink is made by mixing water and juice in the ratio 9 ∶ 7. If x litres of water and 2x litres of juice are mixed in 160 litres of drink, then the new ratio becomes 13 ∶ 15. The quantity of drink (in litres) is:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

A drink is made by mixing water and juice in the ratio 9 ∶ 7.

If x litres of water and 2x litres of juice are mixed in 160 litres of drink, then the new ratio becomes 13 ∶ 15.

**Formula used:**

Initial ratio of water to juice = 9/7

New ratio of water to juice = 13/15

**Calculation:**

Given initial ratio: 9/7

New ratio: 13/15

Total drink = 160 litres

Let x be the litres of water and 2x be the litres of juice added.

Total water = (9/16) × 160 + x = 90 + x

Total juice = (7/16) × 160 + 2x = 70 + 2x

New ratio: (90 + x)/(70 + 2x) = 13/15

⇒ 15(90 + x) = 13(70 + 2x)

⇒ 1350 + 15x = 910 + 26x

⇒ 1350 - 910 = 26x - 15x

⇒ 440 = 11x

⇒ x = 40

Total quantity of drink = 160 + x + 2x

⇒ Total quantity = 160 + 40 + 80

⇒ Total quantity = 280 litres

**∴ The correct answer is option 2.**

questions.question: Which smallest number leaves remainders 4, 5, 6, 7 and 8 respectively when divide by 5, 6,7, 8 and 9 ?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

A number leaves remainders 4, 5, 6, 7, 8 when divided by 5, 6, 7, 8, 9 respectively.

**Formula used:**

If a number N leaves a remainder (divisor - k) when divided by the divisor, then the number is of the form (L.C.M. of divisors) × n - k, where k is the common difference (divisor - remainder).

**Calculations:**

Let the number be N.

When N is divided by 5, remainder is 4. (5 - 4 = 1)

When N is divided by 6, remainder is 5. (6 - 5 = 1)

When N is divided by 7, remainder is 6. (7 - 6 = 1)

When N is divided by 8, remainder is 7. (8 - 7 = 1)

When N is divided by 9, remainder is 8. (9 - 8 = 1)

The difference between the divisor and the remainder is constant and equal to 1 in all cases.

The smallest such number will be (L.C.M. of 5, 6, 7, 8, 9) - 1.

Find the L.C.M. of 5, 6, 7, 8, 9:

Prime factorization:

5 = 5

6 = 2 × 3

7 = 7

8 = 2³

9 = 3²

L.C.M. = 2³ × 3² × 5 × 7

L.C.M. = 2520

The smallest number is L.C.M. - 1:

⇒ N = 2520 - 1

⇒ N = 2519

**∴ The smallest number is 2519.**
